bibliographic.title: Magnetic correlations in polycrystalline Tb0.15Co0.85

affiliations.text: Department of Physics and Materials Science, University of Luxembourg, 162A Avenue de la Faïencerie, L-1511 Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg

bibliographic.abstract: We investigated a polycrystalline sample of the ferrimagnetic compound Tb0.15Co0.85 by magnetometry and small-angle neutron scattering (SANS). The magnetization curve at 300 K is characteristic for soft ferrimagnets but at 5 K the hysteresis indicates the existence of magnetic domains. The magnetic SANS signal suggests that at 300 K the Tb and Co moments are correlated over large volumes within the micrometer-sized grains with correlation lengths > 100 nm. At 5 K, however, the magnetic SANS analysis reveals a reduced correlation length of around 4.5 nm, which indicates the formation of narrow magnetic domains within the ferrimagnet with one dimension being in the nm range. We attribute the observed changes of the domain structure to the temperature-dependence of the magnetic properties of the Tb sublattice.
bibliographic.venue: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics

samples.sample_description: Polycrystalline bulk ferrimagnetic alloy prepared by arc melting.

datasets.dataset_description: Structural properties determined using a Bruker D8 DISCOVER diffractometer with a Co-Kα radiation source.
Magnetic analysis performed on a pellet using a Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS) from 350 K to 5 K in applied magnetic fields up to 4 T.
Unpolarized SANS measurements conducted at 300 K and 5 K within a q-range of 0.06 nm⁻¹ ≤ q ≤ 3.0 nm⁻¹ with applied magnetic fields of 4 T and 0 T.
